slides.heading: String Concatenation
slides.body: String Concatenation is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: String Concatenation
slides.body: String concatenation joins strings together using +. It is useful for building messages from separate text parts.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Concatenation is like attaching two paper strips to form one longer banner.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Join first_name and last_name with a space between them.

quiz.prompt_text: What does string concatenation do in Python?

options: Converts a string into a number
Joins two or more strings together using the + operator
Splits a string into individual characters

quiz.explanation: Correct! String concatenation joins strings together using +. For example, "Hello" + " " + "Ada" produces "Hello Ada".

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to join two strings with a space and print the result.
quiz.explanation: Both string variables must be assigned first before they can be joined with + inside print(). The space in " " separates the two words.

quiz.prompt_text: Join first_name and last_name with a space between them and print the full name.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(first_name + " " + last_name) joins the two strings with a space in between, outputting "Ana Cruz". Always include the space string manually.
